#### 0.4.1 — The `tsc` red is not this repository's, and `exclude` cannot stop it

`tsc --noEmit` exits **1** on four syntax errors, all in
`platform/.next-harness/dev/types/routes.d.ts`. **No lane touched it, no commit contains it, and it
is gitignored** (`platform/.gitignore:9`, `.next-*/`). It is a **torn write**: 154 lines against the
live `.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts`'s 136, with `interface` truncated to `erface` **twice** — a longer
old file partially overwritten by a shorter new one while a harness dev server was running. Its mtime
falls **inside** this gate's own `tsc` invocation.

**Proven environmental, not asserted.** `[gated]` `platform/next-env.d.ts` — itself gitignored
(`platform/.gitignore:52`) and rewritten by Next on every dev run — carries
`import "./.next-harness/dev/types/routes.d.ts";`. With that one line commented out and **nothing
else changed**, `npx tsc --noEmit` prints **no errors and exits 0**. The file was then restored from a
backup and verified byte-identical with `diff`.

**The part worth keeping: `tsconfig.exclude` gives no protection here, and the config looks as though
it does.** `tsconfig.json` excludes `.next-*`, and that exclusion is real but irrelevant — `exclude`
filters which files the *wildcard include* patterns collect, and never which files are reachable by
**import**. `tsc --explainFiles` names the route in one line:

```
.next-harness/dev/types/routes.d.ts
  Imported via "./.next-harness/dev/types/routes.d.ts" from file 'next-env.d.ts'
```

So **any agent who starts a Next dev server with a custom `distDir` silently repoints the type gate at
that dir for every later session**, and a half-written artifact there fails `tsc` for work that has
nothing to do with it. Four such dist dirs now exist (§9). This is a standing hazard on this box
rather than a round-4 event, and it is why the gate table reports `tsc` as **1 raw / 0 source**
instead of quietly picking one of the two.

**The file count is evidence, and the round-4 brief's file-count premise was two rounds stale.**
`[gated]` The brief predicted **878 → 881** on the strength of the orphaned-runners lane getting three
never-executed `tools/` files collected. That arithmetic was already retired in §0.3: those three —
`tools/mobile/{ladder,selectors,settle}.test.mjs` — were un-orphaned in **round 2** (`e9bf33c`), and
the tree has gated at 888, 889 and 890 files since. **878 has not been this suite's file count for
three rounds**, so “still reads 878” could not have been evidence of anything this round. The real
accounting for round 4's +3:

| source | files | note |
|---|---:|---|
| `hud/__tests__/session-end-ledger-close.test.tsx` | +1 | the screen-level pin described above — 31 `expect(`s |
| `lessons/__tests__/finish-work-site-band.test.ts` | +1 | the `finish.ts` lane — 36 `expect(`s |
| `lessons/__tests__/reach-zone-witness.test.ts` | +1 | the `objectives.ts` lane — 60 `expect(`s across 33 blocks |
| `tools/mobile/lib/__tests__/target.test.mjs` | **+0 to vitest** | 89 assertions, and it declares **`node:test`** — so it is the **node** gate's file, and that gate went 19 → 20. The partition audit confirms it: *“913 test files, 893 vitest / 20 node:test, none shared, none orphaned”* |
| **total** | **890 → 893** | 913 across both runners |

**The orphaned-runners lane added zero failures this round, because its work landed two rounds ago.**
All three formerly-orphaned files are collected and green. What the brief anticipated as this round's

owned*.** Neither file appears in any of the eight lanes' `owns` list in

`mapping.ts` reverted to `e9bf33c` and every other round-3 change left in place, both files are
**green — 2 files, 58 tests, 0 failed**. Restoring the two files returns both to red at the same two
assertions. Nothing else in the round-3 tree contributes.

**The mechanism, and why the new behaviour is right and the old tests are wrong.** Lane 4 moved the
repeat-ladder key off the **scenario id** and onto a new **repeat family** (`repeatFamilyForCode`),
because the scenario table is many-to-one and was therefore billing «ПОВТОРНА ГРЕШКА ×1.5» for the
*second distinct fault* taught by one mini-lesson. Both broken tests encode the **old** semantics as
their premise, in as many words:

- `teach-escalation.test.ts:110` — *"the second ev-lane-change hit is already a repeat → graded, not
  taught"*. `LANE_CHANGE_WITHOUT_INDICATOR` and `LANE_CHANGE_WITHOUT_MIRROR_CHECK` are now separate
  families — which `mapping.ts` argues for explicitly (*"the signal and the look are two duties"*) —
  so all three moments teach and `r.taught` is 3, not 2.
- `s-w1-bot-completion.test.ts:428` — *"Both codes map to the same „ev-lane-change" encounter key, so
  the FIRST teaches… and every further fault of that same encounter SCORES"*. With the pooling gone
  the reposition is no longer escalated and the drill now passes.

**This is the aggravating detail: lane 4 measured this exact drive and did not run the test that pins
it.** Its own `mapping.ts` header lists the blast radius drive by drive, including
*"`sc-ln-turn-lane-arrows` late-two-lanes (9 → 6 official, 13.5 → 6 training)"* — the very case
`s-w1-bot-completion.test.ts` asserts. The census was done; the grep for downstream consumers was not.
**Neither failure is a defect in the new code, and neither may be closed by weakening an assertion:**
both tests must be re-premised on the repeat family, by the lane that owns the change.

whose signature is *a test failing in a file no lane owned*; (b) a real defect a new test correctly
caught; (c) a lane that shipped a test file it never ran. All three appeared in wave 3 (§0.2). None
appeared here. This is the first multi-lane round in the programme to land clean.

**No assertion was weakened to get there**, which is the other way this number could have been bought.
`[gated]` Every changed test file gained assertions against `HEAD`: `weather.test.ts` 40 → 62
(14 → 23 blocks), `coach.test.ts` 35 → 54 (12 → 20), `markings-paint-truth.test.ts` 89 → 138
(18 → 29), `sim-overlay-line-grid.test.ts` 40 → 42, `ladder.test.mjs` 9 → 12, `settle.test.mjs` 73 → 73.
No `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `xit` or `xdescribe` appears in any changed or new test file, and no
test file anywhere in the repository — tracked or untracked — is missing `expect(`/`assert`.

**The file count is the evidence, and all ten are accounted for.** The count is *not* 881, which is

#### 0.1.1 — The orphaned-runners lane: a FINDING, not a regression

The lane got **three test files executed that no runner had run since the vitest include glob was
narrowed off `../tools/mobile/**/*.test.mjs`** — a narrowing that was itself correct (the broad glob
was swallowing that directory's node:test files and hard-failing on them) but that left everything
else in the directory claimed by nobody. `[read]` `platform/scripts/tools-tests.mjs` carries the
measurement: at commit `85ca415`, `npx vitest list --filesOnly` returned 878 files and none of them
was one of these three; asking vitest for them **by name printed nothing and exited 0**. Between them
they held **33 test blocks and 88 assertions, green by absence — which is the same green a passing
suite prints.**

**Their red count in this gate is 0, and that 0 must not be read as "nothing was wrong".** One of the
three *was* red on its first ever execution, and the lane repaired it before shipping:

| file | first-run verdict | what the lane judged, and which way |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/mobile/ladder.test.mjs` | **RED** | **the TEST was stale, not the code.** Its geometry pin listed four device profiles while `DEVICES` held six: commit `96a3ea5` (2026-08-11, "a six-phone ladder with real notches") added the two Samsung `galaxy-gesturebar-*` rows and the pin had been wrong for eight days with nothing able to say so. The lane pinned all six **and added a safe-area band assertion**, because `galaxy-gesturebar-portrait` is 360x780 — the same viewport as `small-portrait`, deliberately, as a controlled A/B in which the inset is the only variable — so geometry alone cannot tell the two rows apart, and a silent inset collapse would leave every "measured against an Android 15 gesture bar" claim false while the geometry pin still passed. +2 blocks, +3 assertions. |
| `tools/mobile/settle.test.mjs` | green | header correction only: the comment claiming the config "already globs `../tools/mobile/**/*.test.mjs`" had been false since the narrowing. 73 assertions unchanged. |
| `tools/mobile/selectors.test.mjs` | green | untouched — correct as written. |

**The structural fix is what makes this non-repeatable, and it is the more valuable half.**
`VITEST_INCLUDE` now lives in `platform/scripts/tools-tests.mjs` — plain `.mjs`, readable by *both*
runners — and `vitest.config.ts` imports it. `auditOwnership()` compares the runner each test file
**declares** (read from its imports, with comments stripped first, because half the files here explain
a defect by quoting the code that caused it) against the runners that will actually **execute** it
(vitest's own `tinyglobby`, resolved *through vitest's own package* so the version that answers is the
version that will run, with vitest's own options; plus this script's own walk). It fails on every
disagreement in either direction — claimed by nobody, by both, or by the wrong one — and it runs as a
**precondition** in the node gate, before a single test, as well as a test inside the vitest gate.
Silencing it now takes two deliberate acts in two runners rather than one narrowed glob.

The predicted failure mode arrived: **83 lanes launched, 46 returned, 44 of the planned suspect files
were actually written, and nothing gated any lane against any other.** Third occurrence of the same
process finding (§6.9), and the first at a scale where it dominates the gate.

**Two kinds of red, and they mean different things.** `[gated]` `git cat-file -e 730da10:<file>`
separates them:

- **3 failures are true regressions** — assertions that were **green before wave 3** in test files
  that already existed: `b58-gate-never-over-posted.test.ts` ×2 and `s-w8-bot-completion.test.ts` ×1.
  Some lane changed production code out from under a passing guard.
- **17 failures arrived red in files written by this wave** — `markings-paint-truth.test.ts` (15,
  brand new) and `signals-sweep161.test.ts` (2, brand new). **A lane wrote a test file and shipped it
  failing.** That is not a collision in the fixture sense; for the 8 dash rows and the 3 crashes below
  it is a lane that never ran the file it authored, and the 529 outage explains why nothing caught it
  — the refuter that would have is one of the 69 agents that were killed.

- **`markings-paint-truth.test.ts` × 3 — the fixture dies inside a file no lane owned.** `[gated]`
  `a run too short for one whole dash stays unpainted`, `a shipped skew (18°)…` and
  `skew 90° neither hangs the build…` all die with
  `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` at
  `world/builders/network.ts:415`, `district.intersections.filter(…)`. The markings lane built two
  inline districts through `assertDistrict`, and **`assertDistrict` (`world/types.ts:320`) never
  checks `intersections` or `roundabouts`** though `District` declares both required and
  `analyzeNetwork` dereferences both unguarded. `[read]` All **105** shipped `content/world/*.json`
  carry both fields, so no map is broken — the hole is that the validator returns a `District` it
  never validated. **`world/builders/network.ts` is one of the 39 lanes that never landed** (1
  finding, 1 critical): this is precisely the stated signature — *a test failing on a file no lane
  owned*.
- **`markings-paint-truth.test.ts` × 8 — the instrument is wrong, not the paint.** `[read]` The eight
  `dashed rhythm` rows measure dashes with `clusterAlongS(centre, DASH_LENGTH_M / 2)`. A dash quad's
  corners sit at `mid ± DASH_LENGTH_M/2` — **5.0 m apart in s against a 2.5 m cluster threshold** — so
  every dash counts as two clusters and the assertion sees exactly `2n`: `tj-occluded` 16 for 8,
  `ov-lane` 46 for 23. Where the arm also carries a stop line, that quad lands inside the `|t| < 0.25`
  centre filter *outside* the trimmed run, which is the negative leading margin (`tj-emerge` −0.60 m,
  `sx-v1` −27.93 m) and the extra clusters (11 for 10, 24 for 22). The production `dashStations`
  re-spacing is sound; the measurement needs a threshold strictly between `DASH_LENGTH_M` and the
  fitted gap, and needs paint outside `[s0, s0 + length]` dropped.
- **`markings-paint-truth.test.ts` × 2 — another lane's paint landed in the window being measured.**
  `ov-lane-v1: the осева IS painted` fails on `0.2568 < 0.25` — one centre-line vertex on the S-curve
  sits 0.257 m off axis against a tolerance the test's own comment derives as half of
  `CENTER_LINE_WIDTH_M` (0.1875) but writes as 0.25. `tj-emerge-v1: the Б2 arm carries a solid М7 stop
  line` expects **2** transverse vertices and finds **10** — the same commit changed `paintStopLine`
  to return its real quad count and changed `buildWorldGeometry.ts` (52 lines) alongside it.
- **`b58-gate-never-over-posted.test.ts` × 2 — a stricter rule landed under an older test.** `[read]`
  The B58 lane clamped the advisor card's printed cap to the posted sign. A later lane rewrote
  `lessons/advisor.ts` with `spokenCapKmh`, which is **strictly stronger**: a card may print a number
  only from the halt band, the author's own title, or a sign that binds — otherwise it prints **no
  number at all** (494 of 953 cards). B58's survey regex `/дръж под (\d+…) км\/ч$/` then matches
  nothing, `Number(undefined)` is `NaN`, and `!(NaN <= posted)` books every numberless card as an
  offender. Its sibling row pins the pre-advisor string byte-for-byte
  (`"Стигни зоната — дръж под 52 км/ч"`), which is the behaviour the advisor lane deliberately
  removed. **No product defect in either lane** — B58's two rows must be rewritten to the newer
  contract (*no number, or a number ≤ posted*). B58's headline row still passes.
- **`s-w8-bot-completion.test.ts` × 1 — treat as a regression until proven otherwise.**
  `sc-hz-accident-scene` L3 `mistake-squeeze` scores `["COLLISION","COLLISION"]` where the test pins
  `["COLLISION"]` and `score` 10. That is **the exact defect class §2.1 C3 claims to have closed** —
  one continuous shunt billed as many accidents. A wave-3 `rules/engine.ts` lane moved the episode
  boundary C3 installed. This is not obviously a fixture disagreement and must be judged on the
  engine, not on the test.
- **`signals-sweep161.test.ts` × 2 — treat as a regression until proven otherwise.** `stageActor`
  returns `carDistM` **90** where both `sc-sflash-conflict` (authored offset) and `SC_SIGNAL_DEAD`'s
  own 95 m expect 95. Two independent districts clamping to the same 90 says a placement clamp
  changed, and the test's claim — *the crossing car is held at the distance the spec claims* — is a
  finding, not a fixture. `traffic/staged.ts` was rewritten in this wave.

  `environment/index.ts`. The row it was named for is *not* closed by that (O11 still stands, see
  §2.6 O16), but the callout that it had never been touched is discharged.

### 2.3 — Class B · File opened, finding not addressed: the great majority of the 765

The seven closures in §2.1 land in four files. Everything else in the 53 opened files is open for the
same reason as Class A — nobody addressed it — with the aggravating difference that a reader looking
at the diff will believe otherwise. The counts per file are in the table in §1 and in the per-file
sections above; the closure delta is what §7 says does not exist.

**Wave 3 makes this the document's biggest lie risk.** 44 files were written, ~20,000 lines landed,
and **the closure ledger §7 asks for still does not exist**, so nothing in the tree distinguishes „a
lane rewrote this file and closed nine of its rows" from „a lane rewrote this file and closed none".
The only per-finding closure evidence wave 3 produced is what its lanes wrote about the findings they
could **not** close — §2.6 — which is the inverse of the ledger and is not a substitute for it.

### 2.4 — Class C · Addressed, and the address does not hold

Twelve rows: §4 R1–R8 carried from the previous pass with today's status, and N1–N5 opened by wave 2.
These are the most dangerous rows in the document, because each one has a fix, a test and a paragraph
of prose arguing it — and does not do what the prose says.

### 2.5 — Class D · Cannot be closed by code in this repo

- The two content-signature reds (§8) — a human signature, not a patch.
- The 47 lessons in §5 that have never been judged or never been driven — a reader and a harness.
- The evidence-integrity rows in §7 — a backup path and a bookkeeping field.

**O20 and O21 are the same class as O2/O3, found in a file that had never been opened** — a gate
certifying something no disc can witness. The `objectives.ts` lane was briefed to *judge that claim
yourself; do not inherit it*, and it did: rather than accept “unclosable”, it made the demand
structural — the gate derives what it must measure from the banner the student reads, so **a promise
cannot be written that nothing enforces** — and then filed only the two rows that derivation
genuinely cannot bind, because their banners name a speed while their briefings name the lamps.
That is the difference between a `KNOWN_OPEN` row used as a debt and one used as a permission.

**And every round-4 lane filed at least one row.** After §0.3 recorded that the round-3 lane with the
widest blast radius filed nothing at all, this round has no silent lane — six lanes filed seven rows,
and the two that filed none (`SessionEndScreen`, the partition lane's node half) each shipped a test
that pins what they could not fix. That is the pattern to keep.

**And two round-3 lanes reported nothing they could not close.** Lane 4 (`repeat-key`) and lane 5
(`FaultCard`) filed no open row — and lane 4 is the one that broke two test files it did not own
(§0.3). **A lane reporting no residue is not evidence of none**; in this round it was the lane with
the widest blast radius and the quietest report.

**O2, O3 and O5 are classes, not instances — 16 lessons between them** — and every one is a green
tick a student is shown for a skill the product never measured. That is the same shape as the
document's opening warning (*passing 2 while failing 3*), now with names.

**And the critical lanes that have still never run reported nothing at all.** Their findings have
neither a fix nor a reason: absence of a report there means the agent was killed or never launched,
not that the finding was examined and left. **Round 2 added three reasons and closed none of the ten
wave-3 rows; round 3 added six more and closed one of its own (O14), which was a hole in round 2's
fix rather than a corpus finding; round 4 added seven and closed none of the nineteen before it** —
O1–O10 stand exactly as written, O11/O13 are carried forward as O16/O19, and O16 (weather leaking on
the live path) is now joined by O24 in the same file, which is the second time `weather.ts` has
shipped a mechanism whose reader lives elsewhere.

**Nineteen rows became twenty-six and not one older row closed.** That was the honest reading of four
rounds: the programme is very good at *finding and naming* what a lane cannot reach, and had not yet
built the thing that spends those rows — a lane scoped to a fix that crosses two files. Fifteen of
the twenty-six are one edit each in a named file at a named line.

Fourteen findings were filed against files that cannot contain them. Nothing was wrong with the
findings or with the lane; the *routing* was wrong, and it was wrong because the suspect file was
inferred from the finding's title rather than from its frame. That is a defect in how this document
assigns work, and it is the first time a lane has measured it: **78 % of one lane's assigned bucket
was misrouted.** If that rate holds anywhere else, the per-file counts in §1 and §2.2 are softer than
they look — which is an argument for the committed generator §7 keeps asking for, pointed at
provenance this time rather than arithmetic.

Every lane below was measured by an independent reviewer whose only task was to refute it. `[adversarial]`

whole (C3). The speeding half does not: the write-up claims «eleven rows for one continuous
overspeed… now 10 points», and the run.log's own speed samples are a **saw-tooth** — 49 км/ч with
dips to 1, 5, 6 and 20 км/ч in a zone the HUD shows as 20. Those dips sit at or under the limit, so
`speedReset` fires and `speedingRearmSec: 4` re-arms a **new** bill that `repeatSec: 0` cannot reach.
Replaying all 39 logged samples through the real reducer reproduces the photographed 11 exactly and
then gives **2 (linear) / 6 (step)** after the fix. Directionally right; the headline is wrong by a
factor of two to six, and **the re-arm path is untouched and open.**

**Lane B · `components/sim/TouchControls.tsx` — FIXED, DIAGNOSIS NOT.** C4 and C5 hold. The lane's
§2 explanation of *why* mobile legs are convicted (the four-clock pedal-vs-world ramp) was measured
wrong by the reviewer. What is **not** in doubt and is open: the mobile-only conviction is real and
reproduces today — `sc-zebra-approach · pc · right` = **ИЗДЪРЖАН · 0 наказателни точки · 3/3**,
0 guard firings; the same lesson `· mobile · right` = **НЕИЗДЪРЖАН · 10 точки · 1/3**, «Настъпи
сблъсък» + «Непропускане на пешеходец», 6 guard firings. 217 guard firings on **73 of 97**
`mobile-right` legs against **1 of 98** `pc-right`. The cause is now unnamed again.

  „the shell has not threaded the task cap yet" block asserts the CURRENT mounts, so it goes red the
  moment the thread lands."* `[gated]` `hud/__tests__/governor-cap.test.ts` is **unmodified this round
  and contains no `taskCapKmh`, no „task cap" and no „threaded"**. The block exists — in
  `hud/__tests__/governor-speed-contract.test.ts:218`, *"…and the shell has not threaded it yet, which
  is stated rather than implied"* — and it does exactly what is claimed: it reads `LessonPlayShell.tsx`,
  finds both `<StatusDashboard …/>` mounts and asserts `expect(mount).not.toContain("taskCapKmh")`, so
  it inverts the instant O51 lands. **The mechanism is sound and the address is wrong.** Whoever lands
  O51 will grep the named file, find nothing, and reasonably conclude no tripwire was left. Fix the
  citation; do not weaken the test.
- **The source-text assertions in `governor-speed-contract.test.ts` were checked against this repo's own
  ban and pass it.** The repo has been burned by tests asserting over comment-stripped source (§2.1 C5;
  eight such tests once left 867 green against dead code), and round 10's own lane brief forbade the
  pattern outright for proving publication. Here it is used only to pin **cross-file routing state**,
  which is the established `touchHintLifetime.ts` ⚠ discipline, and the one count that could be spoofed
  by a comment was verified: both `taskCapKmh={taskCapKmh}` occurrences in `StatusDashboard.tsx`
  (lines 704, 812) are live JSX, neither is inside a docstring. The publication proof itself went the
  other way — `hud/__tests__/dashboard-publication.test.ts` drives the extracted function directly and
  `conditions` is a **required parameter**, so dropping the scene's hand-over is a compile error rather
  than a silent winter lesson with no lights row. That is what the brief asked for.
- **The coverage union was rebuilt from `git diff`, and the manifest would have lied by 13 files.** See
  §1 and §2.2. Recorded here because it is a bookkeeping rule, not a finding: **a lane manifest records
  intent, a diff records work, and only the second is evidence.**

  outside `node_modules` returns **nothing**; there is no generator in the tree and there never was

  own rows — which was re-run today and reproduces 1,686 / 1,012 / 318 / 138 exactly. **The prose is

  corpus for this document — **16,272 readable frames and 24 JSONL files** — exists on **one
  7,200 rpm HDD and nowhere else**. Every «A finding without a frame is not a finding» row above is
  one disk failure from unverifiable. No backup path is defined. **Open.**
- **There is still no per-finding closure ledger, and wave 3 made its absence structural.** This is
  why §2 can only be honest at file granularity, and it is now the single largest piece of missing
  bookkeeping in the programme: after **three** waves, 53 files opened and ~20,000 lines landed, the
  answer to *„how much of the sweep is repaired"* is still **„7 named findings of 1,012, in 4 files
  of 138"** — because 44 files' worth of wave-3 work claimed nothing per-finding and nothing in the
  tree required it to. `[corpus]` The fix is unchanged and is now overdue by one whole wave: one
  field on the record — `closedBy` (commit or file:symbol) plus `closedEvidence` (the test that goes
  red without it) — and a rule that no lane may claim a row without filling both. Wave 3's
  `KNOWN_OPEN` arrays (§2.6) show the mechanism works when a lane bothers: a typed list whose
  staleness is asserted is exactly the shape the ledger needs, built by lanes for the rows they
  **could not** close while the rows they did close went unrecorded. **Open.**

errors”.** `[gated]` `.next-harness` is what made `tsc --noEmit` exit **1** in §0's gate table, on
four syntax errors in a half-written `routes.d.ts` inside it. The reason it can reach the type gate
at all is that **`tsconfig.json`'s `exclude: [".next-*"]` does not and cannot stop it**: Next rewrites
the gitignored `platform/next-env.d.ts` to `import "./.next-harness/dev/types/routes.d.ts";`, and
`exclude` filters wildcard *include* matching, never reachability by import. Full proof and the
`--explainFiles` output are in §0.4.1. **This raises the item from housekeeping to a gate hazard**:
any session that runs a dev server with a custom `distDir` poisons `tsc` for every session after it,
and the failure names files no one has touched.

**AND THE ROUND-5 GATE SHOWS WHY „green" DOES NOT MEAN „disarmed" — the hazard is intact and simply
was not firing.** `[gated]` Re-read 2026-08-19 at the round-5 gate, where `tsc --noEmit` exited **0**
with no output at all. Nothing was fixed: `platform/next-env.d.ts` **still** carries

**490 MB**, and the reason the gate passed is that `routes.d.ts` is 4,615 bytes and *complete* right
now (mtime 10:57, minutes before the run) where §0.4 caught it **half-written**. **The type gate's
verdict therefore depends on where another session's dev server happens to be in its write cycle when
the gate runs** — a green that is a race, not a state. It will exit 1 again the next time a gate lands
mid-write, naming files nobody touched, and this is the second consecutive round in which the round's
`tsc` result was decided by an artifact outside the repository. The remedy is unchanged and is one line:
that import is in a **gitignored, Next-generated** file, so the fix belongs in whichever session owns
`.next-harness`, not in a source edit here.
